test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 08 Jan, 2024)
subject: general
question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

She said, “ If only I could relive my past!”

options.text: She said that she could relive her past.
She wished that if she could relive her past.
She wished that she could relive her past.
She wished if she could relive my past.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the form of a wish, which is expressed in the past tense.
 
• The structure **"wished that she could"** correctly **conveys the meaning of a wish about something unreal in the pas**t.
 
• The use of "**if**" is unnecessary in** indirect speech when expressing a wish.**
 
• The correct option is in line with the rules of converting direct speech to indirect speech, particularly for wishes.

Hence, the correct indirect form is** ** **'*She wished that she could relive her past*.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In indirect speech, wishes are often introduced by the verb "**wish" **followed by "**that"** and a clause.
 
• When expressing wishes about the past, the verb in the clause is in the past form (e.g., "could relive").
 
• Example: "***I wish that I could fly"*** becomes "***He wished that he could fl***y" in indirect speech.
